title: What God judges right and counts as righteousness
source_text: VI. Neque dubium esse potest quin illud vere bonum & justum sit, quod recte factum a Deo judicatur, & quod Deus ipse ad justitiam imputat. At fideles quos Dei gratia renovavit, faciunt quae Dei judicio recta sunt, & quae agunt divino spiritu impellente, ad justitiam ipsis a Deo imputantur. Ita 15. cap. lib. 1. Regum, David dicitur fecisse rectum in oculis Domini. Et Deus ipse in eodem lib. cap. 14. Regem Jeroboham per Prophetam increpans, dicit illi, Non fuisti sicut servus meus David, qui custodivit mandata mea, & secutus est me in toto corde suo, faciens quod placitum esset in conspectu meo. Et Psal. 106. Quod zelo accensus Phinees ad iram Dei placandam aggressus est, dicitur ipsi fuisse ad justitiam imputatum. Stetit Phinees, inquit Propheta, & executus est justitiam: & fecit subsistere ultionem: & reputatum est ei in justitiam in generatione & generationem usque in sempiternum.
pass_a_gloss: VI. Nor can there be any doubt that that is truly good & just, which is judged by God to be rightly done, & which God himself imputes for righteousness. But the faithful whom the grace of God has renewed, do what is right in God's judgment, & what they do at the impulse of the divine spirit, is imputed to them for righteousness by God. Thus in chap. 15. of book 1. of Kings, David is said to have done what was right in the eyes of the Lord. And God himself in the same book chap. 14. rebuking King Jeroboam by the Prophet, says to him, You have not been as my servant David, who kept my commandments, & followed me with all his heart, doing what was pleasing in my sight. And Psal. 106. What Phinehas, kindled with zeal, undertook to appease the wrath of God, is said to have been imputed to him for righteousness. Phinehas stood, says the Prophet, & executed justice: & made the vengeance cease: & it was counted to him for righteousness from generation to generation for ever.
pass_b_english: Thesis VI. There can be no doubt that what God judges rightly done, and what God himself counts as righteousness, is truly good and just. Believers whom God's grace has renewed do what is right in God's judgment, and what they do under the impulse of God's Spirit God counts to them as righteousness.

So in 1 Kings 15 David is said to have done what was right in the Lord's eyes. In chapter 14 of the same book God rebukes King Jeroboam through the prophet: 'You have not been like my servant David, who kept my commandments and followed me with all his heart, doing what pleased me.'

In Psalm 106, what Phinehas did in his zeal to turn away God's anger is said to have been counted to him as righteousness: 'Phinehas stood up,' says the prophet, 'and carried out justice, and made the punishment cease; and it was counted to him as righteousness from generation to generation, for ever.'

choices.why: Le Blanc's thesis: the works of the regenerate are truly, not just apparently, good, even though they are not perfect.
